item.title: How a Blue Wave midterm might reshape the AI industry
item.dc:creator: Theresa Loconsolo, Anthony Ha, Sean O'Kane, Kirsten Korosec
item.description: Democrats’ historic victories in this week’s U.S. midterm elections could also transform the tech industry. The public voted on 41 data center-related ballot measures on Tuesday — in all but one, the majority voted to impose more restrictions on data center development. item.title: Harbinger raises $240M after expanding into defense
item.dc:creator: Sean O'Kane
item.description: The Los Angeles-based startup has now raised more than $650 million, and is working on electric trucks, emergency vehicles, and a driverless platform for the military.

item.title: Food delivery startup Wonder files for IPO as it explores its next big bite
item.dc:creator: Lauren Forristal
item.description: Following years of fundraising, acquisitions, and expansion, food delivery startup Wonder is moving closer to becoming a publicly traded company.

item.title: Axiom Math wants to keep AI slop out of mathematics
item.dc:creator: Aditya Mehta
item.description: As AI floods math with unchecked proofs, Axiom Math is betting on verification. The startup’s AI agents just formally verified the Stacks Project, one of the field’s biggest libraries.

item.title: Zipline hits $21.5B valuation as Walmart expands bet on drone delivery
item.dc:creator: Kirsten Korosec
item.description: Zipline raised $1.5 billion and ramped up its partnership with Walmart.

item.title: Aina’s smart ring has a screen, a joystick, and a mic so you can talk to AI agents
item.dc:creator: Ivan Mehta
item.description: Aina's ring can also take calls and help you dictate notes on your Mac.

item.title: A YC startup is putting $1M behind 5 unsolved materials science problems for AI
item.dc:creator: Tim Fernholz
item.description: While frontier AI models have solved a remarkable series of outstanding mathematics problems and made progress in the life sciences, they have yet to truly plumb the complex physics in advanced materials.

item.title: Nothing CEO says company’s mysterious AI-first device is dropping next month
item.dc:creator: Lucas Ropek
item.description: While it's not yet clear what kind of product the smartphone startup is cooking up, Nothing's CEO said the product is designed to leverage AI for productivity gains.
